Title: api-nwm-gcp
description: REST API backed by National Water Model data, developed on Google Cloud Platform

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/api-nwm-gcp is a deployment-focused repository for a REST API backed by National Water Model (NWM) data on Google Cloud Platform. The project documents cloud infrastructure provisioning with Terraform and gcloud, including service accounts, IAM permissions, Artifact Registry, Cloud Build, Cloud Run deployment, and API Gateway configuration. The API is intended to expose NWM-related data access endpoints such as geometry lookup by latitude/longitude, analysis assimilation time series, and forecast data queries with options such as forecast type, reference time, ensemble, COMIDs, and CSV output. The application stack uses FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn, and Google Cloud BigQuery, indicating a Python web API querying NWM data stored in BigQuery. Example materials include a Colab notebook for NWM and USGS streamflow plotting, a Python plotting script that requests forecast records and visualizes streamflow and velocity, and an Apache Beam/Dataflow example for exporting long-range NWM channel routing forecast data from BigQuery to Google Cloud Storage. The repository is most relevant to users seeking cloud deployment patterns, API-based access to National Water Model data, Google Cloud hydrology data services, BigQuery-backed scientific data APIs, and example workflows for querying and visualizing streamflow forecasts.

Title: awi-ciroh-image
description: CIROH JupyterHub image repository

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/awi-ciroh-image is a deployment and environment repository for building a custom CIROH JupyterHub user image using the 2i2c hub-user-image-template pattern. The repository is intended to define and maintain a repo2docker-based Docker image for 2i2c-managed hubs, with automated GitHub Actions workflows to build, test, and optionally push the image to Quay.io. The README describes the workflow for forking/customizing the image repository, editing repo2docker configuration files such as environment.yml, connecting the repository to Quay.io, testing pull requests with Binder, and configuring a JupyterHub to use the resulting image. It also includes notes for maintaining a NextGen National Water Model (NWM) image branch, including feature-branch development, pull requests into the ngen-2i2c branch, and image tag updates after merge.

Title: CAMELS_data_sample
description: Sample data for running neural hydrology examples, and others.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/CAMELS_data_sample is a small sample data repository intended for learning and testing workflows that use CAMELS hydrology data, including neural hydrology examples and other modeling platforms. It mirrors the original 2014 CAMELS directory structure for streamflow and forcing files by including one sample basin from each numbered CAMELS region directory 01 through 18, and limits the temporal coverage to water years 1993 through 2013 to keep the dataset small enough for GitHub hosting. The repository is explicitly for educational and workflow-development use only, not for scientific citation or production analysis; users are directed to the full CAMELS dataset from UCAR or to CARAVAN for citable data sources.

Title: cfe_v1.0
description: CFE is a conceptual rainfall-runoff model with an implementation of the Basic Model Interface.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/cfe_v1.0 is a BMI-enabled implementation of the Conceptual Functional Equivalent (CFE) rainfall-runoff model, a simplified conceptual approximation of National Water Model runoff generation, vadose zone dynamics, lateral flow, and groundwater/baseflow behavior. The model partitions rainfall into infiltration and direct runoff using either the Schaake or Xinanjiang surface water partitioning schemes, routes surface runoff with either GIUH or a Nash cascade, represents soil moisture with conceptual reservoirs based on Clapp-Hornberger soil parameters, routes lateral subsurface flow through a Nash cascade, and simulates groundwater discharge using conceptual reservoir formulations. The repository provides configuration documentation for calibratable hydrologic parameters, soil and groundwater initial conditions, GIUH ordinates, Nash reservoir parameters, runoff scheme selection, rootzone-based actual evapotranspiration options, and coupling flags for soil freeze-thaw effects. It supports multiple build and run modes: standalone CFE using local forcing files, pseudo-framework coupling with AORC forcing and PET modules through BMI, rootzone AET coupling with SoilMoistureProfiles, and NextGen/ngen framework operation with CFE, PET, SLoTH, and optional SoilMoistureProfiles components. The repository includes CMake and GCC build instructions, example workflows using CAMELS catchment data, BMI unit testing guidance for model control, variable, time, getter/setter, and grid functions, and documentation of the model assumptions behind the National Water Model 't-shirt approximation'.

Title: CIROH-open-source-project-template
description: CIROH open source project template

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/CIROH-open-source-project-template is a reusable open source project template for CIROH GitHub repositories. It provides starter documentation, governance, licensing, security, installation, contribution, changelog, and project-health materials intended to be copied into new or existing CIROH software projects. The README includes instructions for installing the template with a shell command that downloads and runs open_source_template.sh, then guides maintainers to replace placeholder content with project-specific information such as description, technology stack, dependencies, installation, configuration, usage, testing, known issues, help, contributing guidance, licensing, credits, and references. The repository includes standard files for CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, INSTALL, SECURITY, TERMS, and an open source checklist covering contributor practices, maintainer responsibilities, documentation quality, CI/testing, dependency monitoring, semantic versioning, vulnerability handling, issue tracking, pull requests, and community engagement. It is not a hydrologic model or data-processing package; its purpose is to standardize CIROH open source repository setup and encourage transparent, maintainable, secure, and community-friendly research software practices.

ciroh_pyngiab provides PyNGIAB, a Python package and Jupyter-oriented workflow for running end-to-end hydrologic simulations with NOAA's NextGen/ngen framework through NGIAB. The repository has two main purposes: building or using a JupyterHub-compatible NGIAB container image based on pangeo/pangeo-notebook for CIROH/2i2c-style notebook environments, and exposing Python wrapper utilities that invoke NGIAB data preprocessing and model execution workflows without requiring users to run shell commands manually. The README documents use of ngiab_data_preprocess to subset hydrofabric domains, generate AORC forcings, and create NextGen realization and routing configuration files, followed by PyNGIAB-based model execution in parallel or serial mode. Example notebooks support NextGen data preparation from catchment IDs, gage IDs, or VPUs using hydrofabric v2.2, AORC 1-km meteorological forcing data, Exact Extract weighting, and generation of realization.json, troute.yaml, and per-catchment model parameter files. Additional examples demonstrate PyNGIAB testing with LSTM-enabled NGIAB inputs and calibration utilities that retrieve USGS NWIS streamflow observations, update CFE and Noah parameter files, run PyNGIAB simulations, evaluate t-route outputs with xarray, and perform SPOTPY SCE-UA calibration using Kling-Gupta Efficiency. The package is configured as a Python project named pyngiab, version 1.1.1, MIT licensed, requiring Python 3.9+ on POSIX/Linux systems.
summary_data.document_type: hydrologic modeling software package and Jupyter workflow repository

Title: Community-Streamflow-Evaluation-System
description: A Novel Research-Oriented Streamflow Evaluation Tool to evaluation hydrological model performance using a standardized NHDPlus data model.

sample_downloaded_paths: Examples/Class Eval_State - Modeled Streamflow Evaluation by StreamStats.md
Examples/Class HUC_Eval - Modeled Streamflow Evaluation by Hydrologic Unit Code (HUC).md
Examples/Class Reach_Eval - NHD - USGS Streamflow Evaluation.md

summary_data.summary_text: Community-Streamflow-Evaluation-System (CSES), also described as ROSET-AWS, is a Python research-oriented streamflow evaluation tool for assessing hydrologic model performance using a standardized NHDPlus/NHD reach data model and colocated USGS/NWIS streamflow monitoring stations. The package is designed primarily for National Water Model v2.1 retrospective evaluation at daily and aggregated temporal scales, using observations from USGS/NWIS parameter 060 and hosted model/observation datasets accessible through AWS S3 to avoid large local downloads. It supports three main evaluation workflows: Eval_State for state-based StreamStats watershed characteristic and land use/land cover analysis, HUC_Eval for evaluating model performance within one or more Hydrologic Unit Code watersheds, and Reach_Eval for evaluating selected USGS stations and their colocated NHD reaches. The workflows load StreamStats, NWIS site metadata, and model predictions; colocate USGS sites with NHD reaches; compute performance metrics including Kling-Gupta Efficiency; aggregate time series at daily, monthly, quarterly, or annual frequency; and provide interactive maps and hydrograph visualizations for comparing modeled and observed streamflow. The examples emphasize identifying regional, watershed, land-cover, drainage-area, and reach-specific locations where model calibration, parameterization, process representation, reservoir operations, or post-processing could improve streamflow prediction. The repository includes Jupyter-oriented getting-started instructions, environment setup for Python 3.9.12, and a broad geospatial/hydrologic Python dependency stack including pandas, geopandas, folium, holoviews, hvplot, hydroeval, hydrosignatures, dataretrieval, pynhd, pygeohydro, streamstats, boto3, s3fs, xarray, rasterio, and related scientific computing libraries.

CIROH-UA/community_hf_patcher is a Python-based repository of scripts, shell entrypoints, and Docker configuration for generating the CIROH Community Hydrofabric, a temporary CIROH fork of Lynker Spatial's NextGen Hydrofabric v2.2 for CONUS. The repository applies compatibility patches intended for CIROH projects, especially the NextGen In A Box ecosystem, until equivalent changes are incorporated into NextGen Hydrofabric v3. Its main workflow builds and runs a Docker container to download the source hydrofabric, apply data and formatting patches, extract a patched GeoPackage and compressed tarball, and optionally upload outputs to an AWS S3 Community Hydrofabric bucket. Current patches correct gage-to-flowpath mappings for about 4500 gages, reformat the hydrolocation table to be GeoPackage/GIS compliant, and add database indices to commonly searched hydrofabric tables for faster queries. The repository also supports generating individual VPU subsets and compressed VPU hydrofabric tarballs. It is relevant for hydrologic data preprocessing, hydrofabric patching, NextGen-compatible geospatial data preparation, gage mapping correction, GeoPackage formatting, Dockerized data workflows, and publishing patched hydrofabric artifacts to S3.
summary_data.document_type: hydrologic data processing and deployment repository

Title: Conferences
description: presentations and posters from the Conferences

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/Conferences is a repository for Alabama Water Institute and Cooperative Institute for Research to Operations in Hydrology conference presentations, posters, and related slide materials. It is intended to collect CIROH conference content in PDF form, including DevCon materials. The repository describes CIROH as a NOAA–University of Alabama partnership focused on advancing water prediction, streamflow forecasting, flood and drought forecasting, water quality, operational hydrologic forecasting workflows, community water modeling, actionable forecast products, and decision support. Listed CIROH DevCon 2024 NextGen Track sessions cover the NextGen Hydrofabric, preparing models for NextGen using BMI, NextGen In A Box, NextGen simulation development tools, cloud workflows for NGEN modeling applications, TEEHR-based exploration and evaluation of streamflow simulations from different model formulations, and actor-based parallelization in hydrology.

CIROH-UA/data_access_example is a tutorial and example repository demonstrating Python workflows for efficient access to National Water Model (NWM) output. The repository centers on a Jupyter Notebook workflow that generates NWM data-access URLs or JSON header URLs, retrieves remote NWM data for user-specified dates, forecast cycles, lead times, variables, geographic regions, run configurations, and feature IDs, then extracts and plots streamflow time series. It shows two related data access patterns: working with remote Zarr/JSON-referenced datasets and downloading/processing NetCDF files. The examples use parallel processing to improve performance when retrieving and extracting data from multiple NWM files, with serial alternatives and visualization steps included. The workflow relies on Python scientific computing and data access libraries such as xarray, fsspec, numpy, joblib, ujson, matplotlib, psutil, concurrent.futures, and multiprocessing, and references the CIROH-UA nwmurl/urlgennwm utilities for generating National Water Model URLs. The repository is intended as a practical instructional resource for users who need to subset, retrieve, process, and visualize NWM streamflow data for selected feature IDs.

Title: datastreamcli
description: CLI-based workflow tool for NextGen Water Modeling Framework simulations

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/datastreamcli is a Python and shell-based command line workflow tool for preparing, validating, executing, and optionally evaluating NOAA NextGen Water Modeling Framework simulations. It automates the end-to-end NextGen Research DataStream workflow: obtaining or accepting a hydrofabric GeoPackage spatial domain, generating or reusing National Water Model forcing file lists, running ForcingProcessor to create catchment-averaged NextGen forcings, generating BMI configuration files from NextGen realization files, validating standard ngen-run packages, executing NextGen through NextGen In A Box Docker containers, and organizing outputs and metadata in reproducible directory structures. The repository is designed for efficient repeated hydrologic simulations using reusable datastream-resources caches, local paths, URLs, or S3 object storage inputs, and supports workflows over VPUs or custom hfsubset domains. It includes documentation for CLI options, standard directory conventions, model support, step-by-step workflow breakdowns, Docker images, Research DataStream production-style runs, and CIROH DevCon workshop tutorials. Supported and documented NextGen model integrations include SLoTH, CFE, PET, Noah-OWP-Modular, t-route, and LSTM Rust, with additional NGIAB models noted as future or pending support. The package also provides Python utilities such as ngen_configs_gen.py for BMI configuration generation, noahowp_pkl.py for Noah-OWP initialization data, configure-datastream.py for configuration generation, and run_validator.py for checking ngen-run package consistency. It integrates with Docker, NGIAB, ForcingProcessor, nwmurl, hfsubset, TEEHR evaluation, AWS S3, and the CIROH NextGen Research DataStream infrastructure.

Title: deep_bucket_lab
description: Model of water in/out of a bucket. Training an LSTM.

summary_data.summary_text: DeepBucketLab is an educational hydrology and scientific computing repository for teaching neural-network-based hydrologic process representation using a synthetic leaking-bucket model. The project provides an interactive Jupyter notebook and modular Python code that generate stochastic precipitation forcing, simulate multiple bucket configurations as ground-truth hydrologic time series, and train a single-layer LSTM model to predict bucket states and fluxes such as water head, spigot outflow, overflow, evapotranspiration, and precipitation response. It is intended for upper-division and graduate students, educators, and learners in civil engineering, Earth science, hydrology, and environmental science who want hands-on experience with deep learning for dynamic hydrologic systems. The workflow includes defining physical bucket attributes, creating train/validation/test splits across bucket configurations and time periods, normalizing data, building PyTorch data loaders, training with MSE loss and Adam optimization, visualizing learning curves and simulations, validating model predictions, and experimenting with sensitivity to data noise or alternative hydrologic scenarios. The repository is accessible through Binder and can also be run locally with a Conda environment. Advanced usage is organized into source modules for data generation, LSTM model definition, model control, validation, and visualization, plus run scripts/notebooks, configuration files, and experiment scripts such as noise sensitivity testing.

Title: DEVCON_SNOW_ML
description: Machine Learning SWE workshop for CIROH DEVCON 2024

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/DEVCON_SNOW_ML is a CIROH DEVCON 2024 workshop and tutorial repository for machine-learning-based snow-water-equivalent (SWE) estimation, focused on optimizing algorithms for the Sierra Snow Model / National Snow Model workflow. The materials introduce data-driven SWE modeling for near-real-time snowpack state estimation relevant to National Water Model updates, with emphasis on 1 km gridded SWE prediction in western U.S. mountain regions, especially the Sierra Nevada. The workbook guides users through environment setup, model methodology, training, prediction, hindcast simulation, extrapolation beyond the training domain, and model evaluation. The modeling framework uses observation and geospatial data including NASA Airborne Snow Observatory lidar-derived SWE, NRCS SNOTEL, CDEC snow observations, VIIRS fractional snow-covered area, and Copernicus DEM-derived terrain features. Notebooks describe a distributed regional ML framework with 23 sub-models, feature development, LightGBM and multilayer perceptron neural network approaches, TensorFlow/Keras training, recursive feature/feature optimization concepts, 75/25 train-test evaluation, water year 2019 hindcast validation, and water year 2022 watershed-scale extrapolation. Evaluation workflows use the Standardized Snow Water Equivalent Evaluation Tool (SSWEET) to compute and visualize hydrologic model skill metrics such as RMSE, R2, percent bias, and Kling-Gupta Efficiency, including temporal, elevation, northness, previous-SWE, and interactive spatial error analyses. The repository is primarily Jupyter notebook-based training material with a conda environment specifying scientific Python, geospatial, machine learning, cloud/data-access, and visualization dependencies.
entities: Standardized Snow Water Equivalent Evaluation Tool

Title: forcingprocessor
description: ForcingProcessor calculates NextGen catchment-averaged forcings from gridded sources like the National Water Model.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/forcingprocessor is a Python scientific software package for converting gridded National Water Model (NWM) forcing NetCDF files into Next Generation National Water Model (NextGen/ngen) catchment-averaged forcing time series. It supports the NextGen Research DataStream workflow by reading NWM forcing file lists, using a hydrofabric geopackage or precomputed weights parquet to define catchment polygons, computing polygon/cell coverage weights with exactextract when needed, and writing NextGen-compatible outputs in formats such as CSV, Parquet, NetCDF, and tar archives. The processor is configured through JSON files specifying forcing inputs, hydrofabric/geopackage or mapping files, storage targets, output file types, verbosity, statistics collection, multiprocessing settings, and optional plotting of NWM versus NextGen forcing variables. It includes utilities for generating NWM forcing filename lists using nwmurl and supports multiple NWM operational and retrospective data sources including NOMADS, Google Cloud Storage, NOAA NWM public S3 buckets, and local paths. In addition to atmospheric forcing extraction, the repository documents channel routing data extraction for q_lateral from NWM channel routing files and t-route restart-related inputs using NWM-to-NextGen mapping, crosswalk, and RouteLink files. Docker support provides x86_64 and ARM64 images based on Amazon Linux with compiled geospatial libraries for reproducible cloud or local execution, including AWS credential mounting and environment-variable authentication. The package depends on hydrology, geospatial, cloud, and scientific Python libraries including xarray, netCDF4, h5netcdf, geopandas, pandas, dask, boto3, s3fs, gcsfs, pyarrow, exactextract, matplotlib, imageio, scipy, and nwmurl. The repository includes examples for CFE/NOM forcing, routing-only channel_rt extraction, and t-route restart file lists, plus CI status documentation for forcing source tests, output options, plotting, weight generation, Docker builds, and DataStreamCLI integration.

Title: forecast_data_overlay
description: Tool for displaying varying types of forecast data simultaneously.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/forecast_data_overlay is a Python/Flask web application for displaying and comparing multiple types of forecast data simultaneously on an interactive map. It was derived from the map application and data request functionality of the NGIAB_data_preprocess repository. The application uses a Flask backend to provide API endpoints and a MapLibre GL JS front end to render forecast data layers, with a browser-based options panel for controlling layer visibility, spatial aggregation scale, rectangular region selection, and time settings. The interface is designed around client-side state management through a local cache so that multiple users can independently configure data requests without interfering with each other. The tool supports reducing dense 1 km forecast grids to coarser scales, limiting displayed data by row/column region bounds, selecting forecast times, toggling map layers, displaying selected regions on the map, and downloading processed displayed data. The project is configured for Python 3.11+ with uv-based environment setup and relies on geospatial, cloud/object-storage, multidimensional array, and visualization libraries including GeoPandas, pyogrio, pyproj, xarray, zarr, netCDF4, dask, s3fs, exactextract, boto3, matplotlib, and Bokeh.

Title: GEE_Workshop
description: A CIROH-support repository to educate new users to Google Earth Engine(GEE)

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/GEE_Workshop is a Jupyter Notebook-based training and workshop repository for teaching new users how to use Google Earth Engine in hydrologic machine learning workflows. The workshop guides participants through creating a Python/Conda environment, authenticating and using the Earth Engine Python API, retrieving hydrometeorological data from Google Earth Engine, obtaining USGS streamflow observations from NWIS, incorporating watershed attributes from StreamStats, processing and resampling time series data with pandas, and building daily training data frames for streamflow prediction. The core tutorial applies NLDAS precipitation and temperature data accessed through Google Earth Engine to predict streamflow at USGS gauge locations such as Red Butte Creek near Salt Lake City, Utah. Later chapters develop and evaluate XGBoost regression models, including train/test splitting, scaling, repeated k-fold cross-validation, hyperparameter tuning with GridSearchCV, feature importance analysis, and evaluation on unseen operational-style data. Hydrologic model performance is assessed with metrics including Kling-Gupta Efficiency, percent bias, mean absolute percentage error, root mean squared error, and mean absolute error. The repository is primarily educational, with chapter notebooks, exercise notebooks, setup instructions, and dependency specifications for packages such as earthengine-api, dataretrieval, streamstats, hydroeval, hydrotools, scikit-learn, xgboost, pandas, numpy, scipy, and matplotlib.

Title: hf_pmtiles
description: Script to convert hydrofabric geopackage to pmtiles + example uses

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/hf_pmtiles is a Python/Docker-based utility repository for converting hydrologic geospatial data from GeoPackage format into Protomaps PMTiles for map visualization and tile serving. The workflow is centered on a Dockerfile that downloads and processes the Lynker Spatial Hydrofabric, converts/merges outputs into a PMTiles archive, and provides instructions for extracting the resulting merged.pmtiles file from the container. The README also points to a map folder containing example styling and usage guidance, and recommends serving the generated tiles locally with tools such as Martin Tiles or the PMTiles utility. The repository is relevant to hydrofabric visualization, vector tile generation, geospatial data processing, and local web map tile serving. Data licensing notes indicate use of Lynker Spatial Hydrofabric and community hydrofabric data under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International terms.

Title: hydromachine-tutorials
description: This repository provides educational material regarding the application of Machine Learning in Hydrology.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/hydromachine-tutorials is a Jupyter Notebook-based training and tutorial repository for applying machine learning to hydrology, especially post-processing National Water Model (NWM) streamflow outputs. The materials focus on educational workshops that explain hydrologic prediction post-processing, uncertainty and bias correction, and model development workflows using observed streamflow and watershed/climate features. The decision tree tutorials cover Decision Trees, Random Forest, and XGBoost for regression-based NWM streamflow post-processing, including data access from Amazon S3, preprocessing, visualization of streamflow, precipitation, temperature, and snow water equivalent (SWE), train/test splitting, scaling experiments, manual and automatic hyperparameter tuning with GridSearchCV, feature importance-based feature selection, model saving with pickle, and evaluation against observations. The neural network tutorial covers developing a bidirectional LSTM in PyTorch for time-series streamflow post-processing, including environment setup with Conda on CIROH/2i2c cloud or SageMaker-style workflows, Git-based code access, S3 data retrieval, temporal train/test splitting, MinMax scaling, lookback window construction, tensor preparation, DataLoader/TensorDataset use, GPU/CPU execution, Adam optimization, and evaluation using MAPE, KGE, RMSE, PBias, and cumulative annual streamflow comparisons. Example datasets are described for Great Salt Lake watershed USGS stream stations and include climate variables, water infrastructure/storage percentage, watershed characteristics, and NWM-related streamflow predictors. The repository is primarily educational rather than a reusable software package, supporting workshops on ML model development, hydrologic time-series prediction, post-processing physical hydrologic model outputs, and cloud-based scientific computing workflows.

Title: hydrotools
description: Suite of tools for retrieving USGS NWIS observations and evaluating National Water Model (NWM) data.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/hydrotools is the OWPHydroTools Python namespace package: a production-oriented suite of modular hydrology tools for retrieving observational and model data, processing hydrometric time series, and evaluating hydrologic forecasts and simulations. The repository is organized as independently installable subpackages. hydrotools.nwis_client provides Python and CLI access to the USGS NWIS Instantaneous Values REST service, returning pandas DataFrames with standardized columns for streamflow, gage height, and other parameter codes. hydrotools.nwm_client retrieves National Water Model streamflow forecasts and analyses from sources such as Google Cloud Platform, Azure Blob Storage, NOMADS, local directories, private HTTP file servers, and generic directory listings, supporting NWM configurations such as short range, medium range, long range, analysis assimilation, Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico products. hydrotools.metrics implements hydrologic model evaluation and forecast verification metrics, including contingency-table metrics such as threat score / critical success index, event-scale metrics such as peak, flashiness, and runoff ratio, and flow-duration-curve generation, bootstrapping, interpolation, recurrence/exceedance analysis, log Pearson Type III curves, and Richards flow variability metrics. hydrotools.events supports event-based hydrometric analysis, including hydrograph event detection by decomposition, Eckhardt baseflow separation, and a simple canopy interception model for event-scale rainfall interception estimates. hydrotools.svi_client retrieves CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index data as tabular/geospatial data for supported years, geographic scales, and national context. hydrotools._restclient is a reusable REST API client framework with asynchronous GET handling, SQLite-backed request caching, retries/backoff, URL composition, alias utilities, and batch requests. The project emphasizes scientific Python workflows using pandas, GeoPandas, NumPy, xarray, Dask, and standardized NOAA-OWP canonical DataFrame labels such as value, value_time, variable_name, measurement_unit, reference_time, configuration, usgs_site_code, and nwm_feature_id. It includes Sphinx/Furo documentation, PyPI package metadata, unit-test workflows, contribution guidance for adding namespace subpackages, and citation metadata for OWPHydroTools version 3.0.0.
entities: USGS NWIS Instantaneous Values Web Service

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/lstm is a hydrologic modeling Python package and Jupyter Notebook repository that provides a Basic Model Interface (BMI) wrapper for Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network rainfall-runoff streamflow prediction, developed for integration with the Next Generation Water Resources Modeling Framework (NextGen/ngen) and the Next Generation U.S. National Water Model. The model adapts NeuralHydrology's CudaLSTM approach through repository components such as bmi_lstm.py and nextgen_cuda_lstm.py, using PyTorch-based trained weights and biases from trained_neuralhydrology_models. It supports running pretrained hourly LSTM models for streamflow prediction on basins with required dynamic atmospheric forcings and static catchment attributes, especially CAMELS-style CONUS basins. Included pretrained examples cover an all-forcings/all-attributes model with 8 atmospheric forcings and 26 static attributes, a limited precipitation/temperature plus slope/elevation model, and an all-forcings plus latitude/longitude/elevation model. The repository includes sample NLDAS hourly forcing and streamflow data for four USGS gauges, CAMELS attribute data and documentation, BMI YAML configuration examples, and instructions for preparing basin-specific configurations with forcing paths, model weights, scalers, warmup/run periods, static basin parameters, and timestep metadata. It also contains ngen_files for copying realization configs, hydrofabric GeoJSON catchment/nexus data, LSTM YAML configs, and forcing data into an ngen project tree so the LSTM package can run inside NextGen. Workflows documented include installing dependencies via conda or pip, installing the package, running `python -m lstm`, using BMI control functions initialize/update/update_until/finalize, unit testing BMI getter/setter/time/grid/model-control functions, and modifying examples for new catchments. The repository also contains analysis materials for applying the LSTM across approximately 10,000 HUC01 New England NextGen catchments, comparing predicted flow duration curves against CAMELS basins, and documenting downscaling of LSTM predictions from gauged CAMELS-scale basins to smaller NextGen hydrofabric catchments.
entities: Next Generation Water Resources Modeling Framework
Next Generation U.S. National Water Model
Journal of the American Water Resources Association

Title: LSTM-Tutorials
description: Developing a LSTM from Scratch

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/LSTM-Tutorials is a tutorial and training repository for learning how to build Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks for hydrologic time-series modeling and streamflow prediction/post-processing. The materials introduce PyTorch-based LSTM workflows, including creating windowed time-series tensors, configuring lookback periods, using TensorDataset and DataLoader for batch training, training on CPU or GPU, and evaluating regression models with mean squared error and Adam optimization. The notebooks use a real streamflow modeling example for USGS NWIS gauge 10155000 in Charleston, Utah, linked to National Water Model NHDPlus ID 10375648, with daily streamflow data loaded from the CIROH AWS S3 streamflow-app-data bucket in parquet format. Tutorials progress from simple univariate streamflow LSTM prediction to using National Water Model outputs as feature inputs for NWM-to-NWIS correction, and multivariate post-processing experiments that add dynamic features and compare model performance. The repository also includes getting-started instructions for cloning the repo, creating conda/mamba virtual environments on CIROH Cloud or other 2i2c cloud platforms, registering Jupyter kernels, installing requirements, and connecting to AWS-hosted data.

Title: neuralhydrology
description: Python library to train neural networks with a strong focus on hydrological applications.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/neuralhydrology is a Python scientific software package for training, evaluating, and extending neural network models for hydrological and environmental time series applications, especially rainfall-runoff and streamflow/discharge prediction. The library is built on PyTorch and uses YAML configuration files to define full experiments, including datasets, basin lists, train/validation/test periods, model architecture, loss functions, optimizers, metrics, normalization, inputs, targets, and logging. It provides command-line tools such as nh-run for training/evaluation/finetuning, nh-schedule-runs for distributing multiple experiments across GPUs, and nh-results-ensemble for averaging ensemble predictions. The package includes a modular model zoo with CudaLSTM, CustomLSTM, EA-LSTM, GRU, MTS-LSTM and shared MTS-LSTM, ODE-LSTM, MC-LSTM, Transformer, Mamba, hybrid conceptual/data-driven models, autoregressive LSTM, and several forecast LSTM variants. It also includes model heads for deterministic regression and probabilistic prediction using Gaussian Mixture Models, Countable Mixture of Asymmetric Laplacians, and Uncountable Mixture of Asymmetric Laplacians. The repository supports hydrologic datasets through a dataset zoo and a GenericDataset interface, with tutorials and examples centered on CAMELS US, hourly CAMELS US extensions, CAMELS-CL, and static catchment attributes. Major workflows documented in the repository include installing the package, preparing CAMELS data, training and evaluating LSTM-based rainfall-runoff models, adding new models, adding new datasets, multi-timescale daily/hourly prediction, inspecting LSTM states and gates for interpretability, pretraining on many basins, and finetuning pretrained models to individual basins. Documentation is built with Sphinx and includes quickstart, configuration reference, model descriptions, API docs, tutorials, and contribution guidance. The project is research-oriented, designed for extensibility in hydrology machine learning, and is associated with the JOSS paper 'NeuralHydrology — A Python library for Deep Learning research in hydrology'.

Title: ngen
description: Next Generation Water Modeling Engine and Framework Prototype (ngiab branch - development version of NextGen)

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/ngen is a development branch of the Next Generation Water Modeling Engine and Framework Prototype, a C++14 hydrologic modeling framework for organizing, coupling, and running catchment-scale to national-scale water model components over a HY_Features-style hydrofabric. The framework takes a data-centric approach in which catchments, nexuses, hydrologic locations, catchment networks, model domains, and reference domains define the spatial and topological structure for exchanging water fluxes, forcings, land-surface states, and model outputs. It supports realization JSON configurations that assign formulations to catchments, define simulation time windows, configure forcing providers, specify output variables, and compose single or multi-module model workflows. A major capability is integration of external models through the Basic Model Interface (BMI), including C, C++, Fortran, and Python BMI modules, with documentation for shared-library loading, registration functions, variable name mapping, model parameters, units, array layout conventions, update_until time control, and multi-module coupling. Included or documented submodules and BMI-compatible models include CFE, TOPMODEL, Noah-OWP-Modular, PET/evapotranspiration, SoilFreezeThaw, SoilMoistureProfiles, SUMMA/SummaSundials, LSTM, δHBV2.0, t-route routing, test BMI models in C/Fortran/Python, and ISO C Fortran BMI bindings. The repository provides build, installation, dependency, testing, and contribution documentation for CMake-based builds, Google Test, Boost, UDUNITS, MPI, Python/pybind11, NetCDF, SQLite/GeoPackage support, and optional routing. It includes workflows for local testing, GitHub Actions automated testing, distributed MPI execution, partition generation, subdivided hydrofabric processing, remote nexuses, and CONUS-scale parallel simulations using GeoPackage hydrofabric data, NetCDF forcings, realization configurations, and optional t-route channel routing.

Title: ngen-cal
description: Tools for calibrating and configuring NextGen

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/ngen-cal is a pre-release Python scientific software repository providing tools, libraries, and workflows for configuring, generating, validating, and calibrating NOAA-OWP NextGen (ngen) hydrologic model formulations. Its main package, ngen.cal, supports automated calibration of NextGen formulations using Dynamic Dimensioned Search (DDS), with changelog evidence of calibration strategies including explicit, independent, and uniform strategies, agent-based execution/evaluation abstractions, configurable objective functions and evaluation periods, restart support for DDS, and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for global-best search. The repository also contains independently versioned Python packages for NextGen configuration workflows: ngen.config for generating, validating, resolving paths in, and programmatically interacting with NextGen realization configuration files; ngen.init_config for describing, parsing, serializing, deserializing, validating, and accessing BMI model-specific init_config files in formats such as JSON, YAML, TOML, and Fortran namelist; and ngen.config_gen for generating catchment-specific BMI model configuration files from data sources such as hydrofabric GeoPackage layers and linked model-attribute Parquet data. The config generation framework uses pydantic data models, hook providers, visitable/builder patterns, and file writers to create configurations for supported BMI modules such as CFE and PET, with roadmap references to additional hydrologic components including Soil Freeze Thaw, Soil Moisture Profile, TOPMODEL, LGAR, SAC-SMA, and LSTM. The codebase targets Python 3.8+ and depends on scientific and geospatial libraries including pandas, geopandas, pyarrow, pydantic v1, matplotlib, hydrotools.metrics, hydrotools.nwis_client, and hypy. Repository documentation covers installation via pip from Git subdirectories, pytest-based testing, contributor workflow, Git branching/release management, semantic versioning for nested packages, and security policy.

Title: ngen-datastream
description: Infrastructure and tooling for the NextGen Research DataStream (NRDS)

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/ngen-datastream contains infrastructure, documentation, and operational tooling for the NextGen Research DataStream (NRDS), a cloud-based system that runs daily NOAA NextGen hydrologic simulations and publishes public forcings, model outputs, configurations, metadata, and community-editable realization files. The repository focuses on AWS deployment and orchestration for NRDS using Terraform, EventBridge Scheduler, AWS Step Functions, Lambda functions, IAM, EC2 execution JSON templates, and GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows for planning, applying, validating, and detecting drift in infrastructure. It supports multiple datastream deployments, including CFE NOM, LSTM, routing-only, restart, and forcing-generation workflows over v2.2 hydrofabric VPUs, with run types such as short_range, medium_range, and analysis_assim_extend. The documentation explains how NRDS data are organized in S3, how community members can contribute NextGen model parameter updates through realization files and issues, and how execution metadata enables reproducibility. The repository also includes shell utilities for checking outputs and retries, collecting metadata, pulling datastream data, and importing Terraform resources. Historical Python tooling for generating VPU execution files is present but documented as deprecated in favor of Terraform templates. Training materials and DevCon workshops demonstrate DataStreamCLI-style workflows for running NextGen simulations from scratch or from reusable resource directories, processing National Water Model forcings into NextGen-compatible catchment-averaged NetCDF files, validating ngen-run packages and BMI configuration files, using Docker containers, reusing hydrofabric resources, and visualizing or downloading outputs with related Tethys/NGIAB tooling. The repository references externalized components such as ForcingProcessor and DataStreamCLI, which have moved to separate repositories, but remains the central infrastructure-as-code and documentation repository for operating and contributing to the public NextGen Research DataStream.
summary_data.document_type: deployment and hydrologic modeling infrastructure repository

Title: ngiab-cal
description: a tool for calibrating NGIAB compliant data packages

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/ngiab-cal is a Python command-line scientific software package for simplifying hydrologic model calibration in NextGen In A Box (NGIAB) workflows. It works with the NGIAB run directory structure to create a calibration directory, generate an ngen-cal configuration file, download USGS observed streamflow data, run calibration through Docker, and copy calibrated parameters back into the model configuration. The tool targets NGIAB-compliant data packages and is designed primarily for single-basin, single-USGS-gage calibration. It uses a modified CIROH-UA/ngen-cal branch named ngiab_cal and a prebuilt Docker image to execute calibration with the Dynamically Dimensioned Search (DDS) algorithm. The generated calibration configuration supports CFE and Noah-OWP-Modular hydrologic model parameters, uses Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) as an objective metric, and manages warmup, calibration, and validation time periods. The package provides a CLI named ngiab-cal with options for specifying the data folder, USGS gage ID, iteration count, warmup length, calibration/validation split, debug logging, forced regeneration, and automatic Docker-based execution. Example workflows include calibrating CAMELS basins after preprocessing NGIAB data packages. Limitations include support only for DDS calibration, CFE and Noah-OWP-Modular parameters, and single-gage calibration using the custom ngen-cal branch.

Title: ngiab-client
description: NGIAB Visualizer

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/ngiab-client is a Tethys Platform + React web application for visualizing NGIAB/NextGen model outputs and NextGen DataStream results. The app, packaged as tethysapp-ngiab, provides an NGIAB Output and Datastream Visualizer with geospatial exploration of hydrofabric catchments and nexus points, interactive time series plots for catchment, nexus, and t-route variables, and visualization of TEEHR evaluation outputs including observed-versus-simulated time series and performance metrics such as KGE, NSE, and relative bias. It supports multiple local model-run output directories through an ngiab_visualizer.json metadata file managed by guide.sh or ViewOnTethys.sh workflows, and it can be deployed in a Docker container using the awiciroh/tethys-ngiab image with mounted persistent directories. The visualizer also integrates with the CIROH NextGen DataStream S3 bucket to search, download, cache, and display forecast/run outputs, using a .datastream_ngiab metadata cache. Development uses a Django/Tethys backend and React frontend with webpack dev-server proxying, Python dependencies for geospatial and scientific data handling such as duckdb, geopandas, xarray, netcdf4, numpy, boto3, and botocore, and JavaScript tooling for React linting, testing, and building. The repository includes instructions for local Tethys setup, PDM dependency management, pytest/yapf/flake8 checks, Node.js 20 installation, npm build/test workflows, and Docker-based runtime configuration.

Title: NGIAB-CloudInfra
description: NextGen In A Box: NextGen Generation Water Modeling Framework for Community Release (Docker version) and GitHub Repo for CIROH IT CyberInfrastructure

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/NGIAB-CloudInfra is the main repository for NextGen In A Box (NGIAB), a Docker-based distribution and user workflow for running the Next Generation Water Resources Modeling Framework (ngen/NextGen) on local or non-HPC systems. It provides guide scripts such as guide.sh, runTeehr.sh, and viewOnTethys.sh to launch containerized NextGen simulations, optionally evaluate outputs with the NGIAB TEEHR integration, and visualize results through a Tethys Platform-based NGIAB Data Visualizer. The repository documents installation on Linux, macOS, and Windows/WSL; Docker image usage for awiciroh/ciroh-ngen-image; the expected NGIAB model run directory structure; NextGen realization JSON configuration; included BMI-compatible hydrologic and land surface models; routing with T-Route; and contribution and support workflows. NGIAB run directories center on a config folder containing hydrofabric geopackages, realization.json, ngen.yaml, and per-catchment BMI model configuration, with generated forcings, metadata, outputs, restart, lakeout, and TEEHR evaluation folders. The container includes or references common NextGen-compatible models and modules including SLoTH, CFE, PET, NOAH-OWP-Modular, TOPMODEL, LSTM, Rust LSTM, differentiable HBV 2.0, SUMMA, and T-Route. The repository also contains archived Terraform documentation for deploying related NextGen In A Box cloud infrastructure on AWS, including VPC/subnet setup, EC2 instances, S3 mounting, IAM policies, EFA options, and user/admin Terraform workflows. It is part of the broader CIROH NGIAB ecosystem and links to NGIAB Data Preprocess, NGIAB TEEHR, NGIAB Data Visualizer, DataStreamCLI, NGIAB Calibration, and upstream NOAA/CIROH ngen and t-route repositories.
entities: Next Generation Water Resources Modeling Framework

Title: NGIAB-HPCInfra
description: NextGen In A Box: NextGen Generation Water Modeling Framework for Community Release (Singularity version)

summary_data.summary_text: NGIAB-HPCInfra provides a Singularity-based high performance computing deployment workflow for NextGen In A Box (NGIAB), enabling users to run the NextGen National Water Resources Modeling Framework on HPC compute nodes. The repository is intended for hydrologists and model users who need a self-contained containerized NextGen environment with simplified execution of local or prepared input datasets. Its README documents requesting an interactive HPC compute session, validating or installing SingularityCE, downloading sample NGIAB datasets from CIROH-hosted S3 locations, and running the repository guide script. The workflow supports attaching input data directories containing catchment, nexus, forcing, and realization configuration files, automatically downloading a compatible Singularity image, and launching NextGen simulations in serial, parallel MPI, or interactive shell modes. Example datasets include AWI-007, AWI-008, and AWI-009, with realization configurations referencing SLOTH, NoahOWP, CFE, and a demonstration LSTM. The repository also references related tools for custom input generation, including NGIAB_data_preprocess and ngen-datastream. Core components include guide.sh for user-guided execution, a Singularity definition file for building the image, and a container entry script template for running ngen inside the image.
keywords: NextGen National Water Resources Modeling Framework
entities: NextGen National Water Resources Modeling Framework

Title: ngiab-teehr
description: A repository for coupling TEEHR with NextGen In A Box (NGIAB) simulation output

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/ngiab-teehr is an experimental Python repository for coupling TEEHR hydrologic evaluation workflows with NextGen In A Box (NGIAB) simulation output. It provides a workflow, demonstrated by example_guide.sh and centered on scripts/teehr_ngen.py, for running TEEHR evaluations against NGIAB/NextGen model results, including support for hydrofabric-based USGS gage handling and t-route output format checks. The repository is intended to package this evaluation workflow into a Docker image published to the AWI CIROH registry, with tagged releases triggering GitHub Actions builds for versioned and latest images. It depends on TEEHR from RTIInternational, along with scientific Python and geospatial/data-processing libraries such as pandas, geopandas, xarray, dask, netCDF4, hydrotools, and Bokeh. Changelog entries indicate early functionality for NGIAB-to-TEEHR integration, hydrofabric version handling, NetCDF/CSV field mapping alignment, and metrics such as Root Mean Standard Deviation Ratio (RSR).

CIROH-UA/ngiab-website is a JavaScript web application repository for a React and Vite-based website related to NGIAB. The project uses React 19, Vite 6, React Router 7, Styled Components, Tailwind CSS, and Axios. It provides standard local development, production build, and preview workflows through npm commands. The README documents configuration for accessing the PePy.tech API to track PyPI download statistics for the NGIAB-data-preprocess Python package, including version-specific downloads, total downloads over the last 90 days, and daily download statistics. Deployment configuration expects PePy.tech API settings to be provided through environment variables or GitHub Actions repository secrets.

CIROH-UA/ngiab-website-staging is a JavaScript React + Vite web application repository used as the staging version of an NGIAB-related website/documentation site. The project supports local development with npm start, production builds with npm run build to a dist directory, and local preview with npm run serve. It is automatically deployed as a staging site at https://docs.ciroh.org/ngiab-website-staging when changes are pushed to the main branch, with documented workflows for syncing changes to the production ngiab-website repository either by direct push to a production remote or by tagged release through GitHub Actions. The repository is primarily website infrastructure and deployment configuration rather than hydrologic modeling code.

Title: NGIAB_data_preprocess
description: Tools to subset hydrofabrics, generate forcings, create default realizations for NGIAB

summary_data.summary_text: NGIAB_data_preprocess is a Python scientific software package for preparing input data and default run packages for NextGen In A Box (NGIAB) hydrologic simulations. It supports both an interactive map application and command-line workflows to select a catchment, gage, VPU, or latitude/longitude point, subset the upstream hydrofabric from the CONUS NextGen v2.2 hydrofabric into a GeoPackage, generate catchment-averaged meteorological forcings from NWM retrospective v3 or AORC 1 km gridded data, and create NGIAB/NextGen configuration files such as realization.json, troute.yaml, and per-catchment model configs. The tool can optionally validate required preprocessing steps and launch a non-interactive Docker-based NGIAB run. Supported model realization options include the default NOAH-OWP-Modular + CFE + SLoTH configuration, Python LSTM, Rust LSTM, hourly and daily dHBV2.0, and SUMMA. It can use calibrated parameters from the Community Hydrofabric S3 bucket when available, otherwise default parameters are used. The repository includes SUMMA base settings documentation covering GRU/HRU parameter files, modelDecisions, outputControl, and soil/vegetation lookup tables. It is intended for macOS and Ubuntu environments, can be run install-free with uvx/pipx-style commands, and depends on geospatial and scientific Python libraries including geopandas, pyogrio, pyproj, xarray, zarr, s3fs, dask, exactextract, numpy, netCDF4, scipy, Flask, Bokeh, boto3, and igraph.

Title: nrds-client
description: NRDS visualizer

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/nrds-client is a Tethys Platform and React web application for visualizing NextGen Research Datastream (NRDS) / NextGen DataStream model output. The app provides a geospatial interface for exploring catchments, nexus points, flowpaths, and CONUS gauges, and supports time series visualization for selected catchments and nexus points. It is designed to help users quickly search, explore, and download forecast/model output stored in the CIROH datastream S3 bucket, including available CFE_NOM and LSTM outputs. The repository includes Docker-based usage instructions for running a prebuilt Tethys container, plus development setup guidance for a React frontend proxied to a Tethys/Django backend. Python dependencies indicate support for geospatial and scientific data handling with GeoPandas, xarray, pandas, pyarrow, fsspec, s3fs, pyproj, h5netcdf, and NumPy. The project also includes PDM-based Python dependency management, pytest testing, flake8/yapf linting and formatting, and npm/webpack workflows for building, linting, and testing the React frontend.

Title: nrds-onprem
description: NRDS Onpremise setup

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/nrds-onprem is intended to contain an on-premise setup for NRDS, but the repository dossier currently consists primarily of generic open-source project template documentation. The README, INSTALL, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, and SECURITY files provide placeholder guidance for project description, dependencies, installation, configuration, usage, testing, contribution workflow, semantic versioning, licensing, and vulnerability handling. No concrete NRDS deployment scripts, infrastructure configuration, hydrologic workflows, software components, dependencies, or operational instructions are present in the provided files.

Title: NWM_ML
description: A Machine Learning extension processor coupling the NWM to water resources management tools in the western US.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/NWM_ML is a Jupyter Notebook-based hydrologic machine learning workflow for developing an extension processor that corrects or augments NOAA National Water Model streamflow predictions for water resources management in the western United States. The prototype focuses on the Great Salt Lake basin, with planned scaling to the Upper Colorado River Basin, and is motivated by extending the 30-day NWM operational product toward season-to-season water supply forecasting. The repository describes coupling trained models with Great Salt Lake integrated model wetlands and lake modules to support management decisions involving environmental flows, agriculture, urban demand, and infrastructure-influenced hydrology. Workflows include data preparation from USGS NWIS streamflow observations, NWM retrospective daily flows, StreamStats catchment attributes, USBR reservoir storage, NRCS SNOTEL snow-water-equivalent, NLDAS or NOAA Analysis of Record precipitation and temperature, and seasonal sine/cosine indices. Modeling notebooks cover MLP, bidirectional LSTM, multi-station LSTM, 1D CNN, and XGBoost approaches, with train/test/validation dataset creation, feature scaling, optional feature selection, optional removal of headwater stations, repeated model training and evaluation, and final result saving. Supporting materials include guidance for creating a PyTorch GPU conda/mamba environment, installing a Jupyter kernel, working on HPC platforms, and accessing project data on AWS S3. Temporary notebooks also indicate utilities for moving JSON, pickle, CSV, text, ZIP, and VIIRS TIF files between local storage and S3.
entities: NOAA Analysis of Record for Calibration

Title: nwmurl
description: This library contains utility functions to generate National Water Model data URLs

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/nwmurl is a Python data access utility package for generating National Water Model (NWM) data URLs. The library supports construction of URL lists for both operational and retrospective NWM datasets, enabling users to retrieve or reference NWM files for analysis, modeling, and visualization workflows. Operational URL generation can be customized by date range, forecast cycle, lead time, variable type, geographic domain, run configuration, dataset host/base URL, ensemble member, and optional output-to-file behavior. Supported operational variables include channel routing, land, reservoir, terrain routing, and forcing data; supported domains include CONUS, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico; supported run configurations include short range, medium range, long range, analysis-assimilation, no-data-assimilation, and extended/long analysis-assimilation variants. Retrospective URL generation supports date ranges, selected object types such as forcing and model_output, selected variable/file types such as CHRTOUT, GWOUT, LAKEOUT, LDASOUT, RTOUT, and LDASIN, and multiple retrospective storage locations. The package is installable with pip as nwmurl, distributed via setup.py, licensed under MIT, and depends on Python packaging and utility libraries including python-dateutil, requests, tqdm, gevent, pytest, setuptools, and wheel. It is intended to simplify programmatic access to NWM data hosted on NOAA NOMADS, NOAA public cloud buckets, Google Cloud Storage, Amazon S3, and CIROH-hosted NWM Zarr copies.

Title: OPG-CNN-Northern-Utah-CIROH-Workshop
description: This workshop offers participants an introduction to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for their application in hydro-meteorology. The hands-on portion of the workshop focuses on customizing a CNN through hyperparameter exploration, adjusting CNN layers, and manipulating inputs.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/OPG-CNN-Northern-Utah-CIROH-Workshop is a hands-on training repository for a CIROH workshop on using convolutional neural networks for hydro-meteorological downscaling in complex terrain. The repository teaches participants how to build, customize, train, evaluate, and interpret a TensorFlow/Keras CNN that predicts daily orographic precipitation gradients (OPGs) for Northern Utah from ERA5 atmospheric predictor fields. The scientific workflow uses winter-season data from 1988-2017, including Bohne et al. OPG climatology, GHCND precipitation observations, topographic facets, and ERA5 variables such as integrated vapor transport, accumulated precipitation, 700 hPa temperature, 700 hPa winds, and 500 hPa geopotential height. The notebooks introduce facets and OPGs, inspect NetCDF and tabular datasets with xarray and pandas, standardize atmospheric predictors and OPG targets, split data into training/validation/testing subsets, and train CNN regression models using convolutional layers, max pooling, dropout, batch normalization, dense layers, early stopping, learning-rate adjustments, and loss functions such as mean squared error and mean absolute error. The workshop also includes model evaluation and explainable AI exercises, including feature maps and Grad-CAM heatmaps to identify influential atmospheric regions, followed by a downscaling demonstration that uses predicted OPGs and elevation relationships to create finer-scale precipitation estimates over Northern Utah. The repository is designed for use in the CIROH 2i2c JupyterHub environment or on a personal computer via a conda environment, and includes environment configuration for Python 3.11 with TensorFlow CPU, Keras, xarray, netCDF4, pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, Cartopy, Shapely, and related geospatial/scientific Python libraries.

CIROH-UA/PINN_workshop_ciroh is a training materials and tutorial repository for the CIROH Development Conference 2024 focused on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for solving differential equations and hydrology-related PDE problems. The repository introduces PINN concepts, including embedding physical laws into neural-network loss functions to reduce data requirements and improve physically consistent predictions. It contains Jupyter notebook tutorials for a one-dimensional transient heat equation PINN and a two-dimensional transient shallow water equation inverse problem using sparse observations generated by an RK4 numerical solver. The shallow water notebook formulates conservation of mass and x/y momentum equations for water height and velocity components and trains a PINN with PDE residual and data losses. The heat equation notebook demonstrates automatic differentiation, boundary and initial condition enforcement, and PyTorch training for a HeatPINN model. Additional example folders provide educational PINN implementations for Burgers' equation, a damped harmonic oscillator, the logistic equation, the nonlinear Schrodinger equation, channel flow, and laminar Navier-Stokes flow in a sudden-contraction channel. The laminar-flow material discusses Navier-Stokes equations, stress tensor reformulation, pressure recovery, stream function velocity representation, and references an original TensorFlow 1 implementation and related paper. The repository is configured with a Conda environment using Python 3.11, PyTorch CPU, NumPy, Matplotlib, Jupyter/IPython tooling, tqdm, SymPy, and related scientific Python dependencies.

RIVR is a Flutter/Dart mobile application for river flow monitoring, NOAA National Water Model forecast access, and flood risk assessment for civilian and professional users. The app provides interactive Mapbox-based river reach selection, favorites management, real-time and forecast streamflow views, flood risk categories, return period threshold comparisons, hydrographs, cached/offline-capable data access, user authentication, settings, and push notification alerts for high-flow or flood-risk conditions. It integrates NOAA National Water Prediction Service/NWPS APIs for short-range, medium-range, and long-range streamflow forecasts, a CIROH NWM return-period API for flood thresholds, Firebase services for Auth, Firestore, Cloud Messaging, Analytics, Crashlytics, and TypeScript Firebase Cloud Functions for scheduled river alert checks. The repository includes extensive architecture documentation describing a layer-first clean architecture with models, services, UI layers, ServiceResult error handling, entity/DTO separation, repository coordinators, datasources, GetIt dependency injection, Provider/ChangeNotifier state management, stale-while-revalidate caching, progressive non-blocking forecast loading, retry/fallback logic for NOAA API reliability, and testing strategy. It also contains release, store submission, security, accessibility, and audit documentation for Android and iOS deployment, including app store asset requirements, release checklists, and cloud function deployment history.

Title: rs_route
description: Experimental rust MC routing

summary_data.summary_text: rs_route is an experimental Rust implementation of Muskingum-Cunge channel routing for the NOAA NextGen hydrological modeling framework, inspired by t-route. It provides a command-line routing application that reads NextGen run directories, uses hydrofabric GeoPackage inputs for network topology and channel parameters, ingests NextGen model output CSVs, and writes routing outputs including t-route-compatible NetCDF files and CSV output. The software supports multiple Muskingum-Cunge routing kernels, including a pure Rust implementation, modernized Fortran t-route bindings, legacy Fortran t-route bindings, and a C implementation. Its routing engine uses parallel wave-front routing with topological ordering to process independent network branches concurrently. The repository is organized as a Rust scientific software package with modules for CLI handling, configuration, network/database operations, node state tracking, routing orchestration, CSV and NetCDF I/O, simulation result storage, and kernel dispatch/FFI bindings. It is intended for routing workflows in NextGen hydrologic modeling environments and includes a small integration test dataset.

CIROH-UA/rust-lstm is an active-development Rust implementation of a Basic Model Interface (BMI) adapter for LSTM-based streamflow prediction. It is intended as a faster drop-in replacement for Python BMI LSTM adapters used in CIROH-UA/lstm, NOAA-OWP/lstm, and jmframe/lstm, especially within NextGen framework configurations and NextGen-In-A-Box workflows. The package uses the Burn deep learning framework and bmi-rs Rust BMI bindings, supports ensemble model configurations, and is designed to run PyTorch-trained LSTM hydrology models compatible with the neuralhydrology-style one-layer LSTM plus linear layer architecture. PyTorch model weights from jmframe/lstm or NextGen-In-A-Box are converted automatically to Burn format on first run. The repository documents build and deployment steps using Rust 2024, Cargo, a local bmi-rs clone, Astral UV, and Docker-based patching into CIROH NextGen-In-A-Box images. It produces a shared library, librust_lstm_1025.so, registered in NextGen as a bmi_c/bmi_rust module via register_bmi_lstm for the output variable land_surface_water__runoff_depth.

Title: SWEML
description: Deep Learning national scale 1 km resolution SWE prediction model

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/SWEML is a Jupyter Notebook-centered hydrologic machine learning repository for Snow Water Equivalent Machine Learning (SWEML), a deep learning workflow that predicts 1 km gridded snow water equivalent (SWE) across selected western U.S. mountain regions, with emphasis on the Sierra Nevada, Colorado Rockies, Wind River Range, and Upper Colorado River Basin. The repository combines model documentation, tutorial notebooks, data preparation workflows, model training examples, hindcast simulations, and evaluation notebooks. The SWEML/NSM pipeline assimilates snow observations from NRCS SNOTEL and California CDEC monitoring sites, training and validation data from NASA Airborne Snow Observatory and snow course surveys, terrain attributes from Copernicus 90 m DEM, and engineered features such as water year week, latitude, longitude, elevation, northness, current and previous SNOTEL/CDEC SWE, delta SWE, and previous gridded SWE. The modeling framework divides the western U.S. domain into regional sub-domains to handle different snow climate regimes and supports regionally optimized machine learning models, especially TensorFlow/Keras multilayer perceptron neural networks, with LightGBM/gradient boosted decision trees referenced for feature optimization and model development. Workflows include geospatial preprocessing, feature engineering, HDF5/CSV data handling, training/test splits, 2019 water year hindcast simulation, weekly inference, and interactive visualization of SWE predictions. Model evaluation is performed with the Standardized Snow Water Equivalent Evaluation Tool (SSWEET), using metrics such as percent bias, R2, Kling-Gupta Efficiency, RMSE, physical error, percent error, elevation/time/northness diagnostics, parity plots, and spatial maps. The repository also includes GeoSMART/Jupyter Book tutorial chapters on motivation, methods, data preparation, model development, training, evaluation, workflow management with GeoWeaver, reproducibility, and conclusions, plus environment setup files for conda/mamba, Binder, and Python requirements. Additional notebooks demonstrate programmatic access to NASA NSIDC DAAC Earthdata using spatial/temporal filters and customization services. Overall, the repository is both a research model implementation and educational tutorial for machine-learning-based SWE estimation, hindcasting, and evaluation in snow-dominated hydrologic regions.
entities: Standardized Snow Water Equivalent Evaluation Tool
summary_data.document_type: hydrologic machine learning model and tutorial repository

Title: t-route
description: Tree based hydrologic and hydraulic routing (ngiab branch - development version)

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/t-route is a Python, Cython, and Fortran scientific hydrologic modeling repository for T-Route, a tree-based channel and reservoir routing framework developed for the National Water Model and NextGen hydrologic modeling workflows. T-Route computes streamflow on vector-based river networks from lateral inflow time series while enforcing upstream-to-downstream topological ordering across directed acyclic channel graphs. It supports NHD/NHDPlus-style National Water Model networks and OGC WaterML 2.0 HY_Features network representations, with command-line execution through `python -m nwm_routing` and BMI-oriented workflows for NextGen. Core routing capabilities include Muskingum-Cunge channel routing, diffusive wave routing, dynamic wave support described in the project overview, hybrid Muskingum-Cunge/diffusive routing, levelpool reservoir routing, RFC reservoir forecasting, streamflow data assimilation, and USGS/USACE reservoir data assimilation configuration pathways. The repository is organized into packages for configuration validation (`troute.config` using Pydantic), network preprocessing and graph traversal (`troute.network`), routing kernels and fast reach calculations (`troute.routing`), and National Water Model orchestration (`nwm_routing`). It includes Fortran routing engines wrapped as Python extensions, Cython acceleration, NetCDF-based I/O, YAML configuration files, sample configurations for Muskingum-Cunge and waterbody simulations, V3 configuration documentation, and demonstration/test data for a Lower Colorado River, Texas Analysis and Assimilation workflow. Documentation describes installation on Linux/WSL and macOS, building NetCDF-Fortran dependencies, compiling kernels, running examples, parallel routing strategies such as serial, by-network, by-subnetwork just-in-time, clustered JIT, and diffusive subnetwork routing, and CONUS-scale graph-based routing performance considerations for operational National Water Model use.

Title: Tethys-CSES
description: This repository serves as an interactive evaluation platform to visualize modeled streamflow.

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/Tethys-CSES is a Python Tethys Web Application for the Community Streamflow Evaluation System (CSES), an interactive platform for visualizing and evaluating modeled streamflow against in situ USGS/NWIS monitoring observations. The application supports hydrologic model performance assessment using a standardized NHDPlus-based data model and currently emphasizes National Water Model v2.1 retrospective streamflow evaluation, with NWM v3.0 planned. It provides web-based evaluation workflows for states, individual reaches, and HUC identifiers, allowing users to choose locations, models, and date ranges and view interactive model-versus-observation performance visualizations. The platform is intended to make hydrologic model benchmarking more accessible, reproducible, and useful for researchers and operational practitioners, with initial examples including Alabama, southern Utah NWIS sites, the Jordan River Basin, and Great Salt Lake Basin model evaluation. CSES leverages colocated USGS/NWIS observations from 1980–2020 and model outputs hosted by the Alabama Water Institute on AWS S3 to avoid slow repeated downloads and support faster evaluation. The repository contains the Tethys app packaging configuration and documentation for deploying and using the web application within the broader CIROH community streamflow evaluation effort.
entities: Cooperative Institute for Research to Operations in Hydrology

Title: training-data-workflows-101
description: Data Workflows 101

summary_data.summary_text: CIROH-UA/training-data-workflows-101 is a training materials repository for a Data Workflows 101 workshop focused on teaching reproducible, modular, maintainable scientific Python workflows for hydrologic data analysis. The notebooks guide learners from conceptual workflow design through implementation of a simple streamflow data workflow: acquire and filter data, manipulate or resample time series, and visualize results. The materials emphasize software engineering practices for research code, including functions, variable scope, modular workflow stages, standardized interfaces between modules, code reuse, command-line execution, and moving exploratory notebook code into reusable .py scripts. Hydrology-specific examples include acquiring USGS NWIS instantaneous streamflow using the dataretrieval Python package and acquiring National Water Model Retrospective data using Zarr/xarray patterns, then comparing time series and addressing unit conversion. The workshop also introduces common scientific Python tools such as pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, seaborn, HoloViews, Plotly, and xarray, and discusses practical data workflow concerns including time zones, units, sampling rates, spatial resolution, projections, memory-efficient data access, and selecting only needed subsets from large datasets. The repository is intended for CIROH/JupyterHub-based instruction and includes guidance for running workflows from the terminal with command-line arguments, plus pointers to related CIROH resources such as nwmurl, TEEHR, NETWA, Boto3, THREDDS, and PyViz tools.
